newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-BARCELONA CUT REAL'S LEAD AS CHASING PACK FALTERS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BARCELONA CUT REAL'S LEAD AS CHASING PACK FALTERS.

text.p: Beleaguered Barcelona coach Bobby Robson saw his side reduce Real Madrid's lead at the top of the Spanish league to six points after hanging on for a 1-0 win over Racing Santander on Sunday.
Barcelona (50) move four points ahead of third-placed Real Betis, who drew 2-2 at Real Madrid on Saturday. A further five points back are Deportivo Coruna, who drew 0-0 at home with Atletico Madrid.

Robson's side went ahead at the end of the first half when Luis Enrique Martinez knocked in a free-kick from Angel Cuellar, but were forced to struggle towards the end when striker Juan Pizzi was sent off for a heavy challenge on fellow Argentine Gabriel Schurrer.
Pizzi had only been on the field for two minutes after replacing former Betis striker Cuellar.

Robson's decision to use Cuellar - who was playing his first match since October - together with the reappearance of former reserve team player Albert Celades has been seen as an attempt to change direction.
Barcelona fans have been particularly critical of the sidelining of home-grown players like Celades and Ivan de la Pena in favour of imported stars.

The race for the title and runner's up spot - both carrying automatic entry to the Champions' League - looks increasingly to be between the current top three place after the fourth, fifth and sixth-placed sides all played out goalless draws.

Real Sociedad are five points behind Betis after coming home from Sporting Gijon with a point, but surrendered fourth position on goal difference to Deportivo Coruna, who had the better of their game with sixth-placed Atletico Madrid.

Deportivo should have celebrated the debut of new coach Carlos Alberto Silva with a hatful of goals in the first half, but lost their rhythm after defenders Miroslav Djukic and Nourredine Naybet were hurt colliding with each other.
Djukic, who had to be stretchered from the field, broke his nose and is expected to undergo an operation on Monday.
Reigning champions Atletico are a further point back -- 16 points adrift of neighbours Real -- with Valladolid a further three behind in seventh after a 2-1 win over Espanyol.
Athletic Bilbao moved up to eighth thanks to a splendid hat-trick from striker Ismael Urzaiz in the 3-2 win over Oviedo.
At the other end of the table, Extremadura moved off the bottom for the first time since the beginning of the season thanks to a late goal in the 1-0 win over Rayo Vallecano.
Extremadura fans had greeted the arrival of match officials by waving black handkerchiefs in a protest against recent refereeing decisions.
